source: Guo, Yin, Sun, Chen (2024) Empirical study of problem-solution co-evolution in human-GAI collaborative conceptual design (DRS2024)
finding: Twenty design students did two 30-minute concept tasks with ChatGPT 3.5, Midjourney, both, or no AI. Coded as problem-solution co-evolution transitions plus abduction, deduction, induction. Experts rated outputs. Every AI group beat the no-AI group on creativity.
numbers: N=20 (5 per group: A ChatGPT, B Midjourney, C both, D none). 686 transition segments, 1322 inference behaviours. Mean of 5 creativity metrics (7-point): Midjourney 4.336 (SD 1.62), ChatGPT 4.236 (1.41), both 4.1 (1.54), no AI 3.588 (1.27). Regression vs no AI: ChatGPT +0.648 (p<.05), Midjourney +0.748 (p<.01), both +0.512 (p<.10). Expert kappa mean 0.66, 5 experts, 40 concepts.
limits: Tiny groups, novices only, GPT-3.5, stepwise regression with many marginal p values. Combining two tools gave lower feasibility and usability, unexpected.
agent_relevance: Co-evolution (cross-space moves) is a measurable unit of designerly reasoning. Tool use changed which reasoning type dominated, so scaffold choice shapes thinking, not only output.

source: Guo et al. (2024) same paper, abduction mediation result
finding: Abductive reasoning mediated the AI effect on creativity. Midjourney raised abduction a lot, and abduction predicted creativity. After controlling for abduction the direct Midjourney effect turned negative.
numbers: Abduction vs no AI: ChatGPT +7.2 units (p<.10), Midjourney +27.2 units (p<.01), both n.s. Each unit of abduction adds 0.058 creativity (p<.01). Direct Midjourney effect after control: -0.833 (p<.01).
limits: Mediation from observational coding on n=20; reasoning-type coding used indicator words, a crude proxy.
agent_relevance: Supports an operator that explicitly generates hypotheses about what the problem could be (abductive step) rather than refining the first idea. Deduction-heavy no-AI groups refined more than generated.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Leveraging LLMs to emulate the design processes of different cognitive styles (AHFE)
finding: GPT-4o with a zero-shot chain-of-thought CO-STAR prompt was told to act as a problem-driven or solution-driven designer. Static focus matched human designers, but the model did not copy the human back-and-forth between problem and solution space.
numbers: 4 groups x10 runs (problem-driven / solution-driven, with and without constraints) plus 2 baseline groups x10. FBS coding by 2 coders, agreement 79.5%. Problem-driven runs: Formulation 31.7% vs 16.3% (t=8.489, p<.001); Structure 10.6 vs 29.3 (p<.001). All problem-driven runs had P-S index >1; all solution-driven runs <1 except 2 under constraint. Unconstrained problem-driven runs had fewer PS and SP transitions than solution-driven (p<0.01).
quote: LLMs tend to maintain a sustained focus on one space at a time
limits: GPT-4o only, one task (bathroom product), 2 raters (Pearson r 77%), small n=10 per cell. The authors suggest Graph of Thoughts as a fix.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that single-pass LLM design runs are linear. Cross-space transitions (P to S, S to P), the core of Cross's designerly knowing, must be forced by the loop, not hoped for from a prompt.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) same paper, outcome quality
finding: Cognitive-style process prompts beat a plain baseline prompt on novelty and completeness. Constrained problem-driven designs were no more feasible than baseline.
numbers: Novelty: both styles beat baseline (p<0.05); unconstrained higher than constrained. Feasibility: all groups beat baseline except P2 (problem-driven, constrained). Integrity: both beat baseline (p<0.05); solution-driven always more complete. Scale 1-7, 2 experts. Baseline under constraints was least feasible.
limits: Effect sizes not reported in text read; expert-rated, tiny n.
agent_relevance: A cheap prompt-level process scaffold (state the style and its steps) lifted novelty and completeness. Matching style to task (problem-driven for ill-defined briefs) is a candidate operator choice.

source: Anon (2025) A framework for LLM-powered design assistants
finding: Conceptual framework with three modes: idea exploration, dialogue with designers, design evaluation. Builds on Simon, Cross, Dorst and Cross, Lawson. Designer keeps control.
numbers: No experiments, no numbers.
limits: Pure position paper. Claims such as bias mitigation are asserted not tested.
agent_relevance: Useful only as a map of roles; do not cite as evidence. Shows the field treats co-evolution (Dorst and Cross 2001) as the reference model for LLM design help.

source: Zhang and Qian (2025) From copilot to co-thinker: LLMs in the designer's evolving thinking flow (ADIC 2025)
finding: Three Chinese industry case studies (brand strategy, product innovation, UX research) mapped onto the Double Diamond. LLM roles shifted: macro-scanner in research, creative provocateur in concept design, reflective partner in improvement.
numbers: 3 cases, no quantitative measures.
limits: Qualitative, no controls, authors tied to the cases.
agent_relevance: Suggests the LLM role should change by stage (scan, provoke, reflect) rather than one fixed persona. Weak evidence, but a hint for stage-dependent operators.

source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) The effects of generative AI on design fixation and divergent thinking (CHI 2024)
finding: Sixty people sketched chatbot avatars after seeing an example. Those who got Midjourney images fixated more on the example's features than those with image search or nothing. They also produced fewer, less varied, less original ideas. Fixation moved from the example onto the AI images.
numbers: N=60 between-subjects, 3 conditions (none, Google image search, Midjourney). Fixation (binomial, 14 features): GenAI +.32 (89% CI .11 to .55, BF 124); image search +.27 (BF 42.5). Fluency GenAI -.21 on log scale (BF 3.2, 76% posterior). Originality GenAI -.03 (CI -.06 to -.01). Moderate positive correlation between fixation in AI images and in sketches.
limits: One visual task, students, Bayesian multilevel model with modest effects; read full text this session.
agent_relevance: Fixation, a central designerly failure (Cross), is not cured by generative AI and can be caused by it. A scaffold should not show one polished candidate first; ask for divergent sets before any anchoring example.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Understanding design fixation in generative AI
finding: Argues GenAI shows its own design fixation: it repeats familiar forms. Ten designers used ChatGPT (GPT-4o) and Midjourney for 30 minutes on office chairs. ChatGPT output used fewer unique terms than Red Dot award chairs.
numbers: N=10 (age 22.7). Unique-term proportion: Red Dot 78.2% vs ChatGPT 67.4%. 7 of 10 (ChatGPT) and 8 of 10 (Midjourney) noticed repetition. About 30% (3) asked ChatGPT for ideas first. Experienced designers rejected suggestions; novices adopted them.
limits: Small, word-count proxy for diversity, no inferential test on the 78.2 vs 67.4 gap.
agent_relevance: Model fixation is real and shows up as vocabulary narrowness. A loop can measure it cheaply (unique-term ratio) and trigger a reframe operator.

source: Ma, Grandi, McComb, Goucher-Lambert (2023) Conceptual design generation using large language models (IDETC)
finding: GPT-3 produced 100 solutions for each of 12 design problems and was compared with Mechanical Turk crowd solutions. Experts rated the LLM higher on feasibility and usefulness and lower on novelty. LLM sets repeated themselves after a few items.
numbers: 12 prompts; 600 solutions rated by 2 experts (0-2 scales); few-shot prompts gave mean cosine similarity to crowd 0.804 (SD 0.06), zero-shot with 'unique' 0.746. Adding 'diverse' to prompt 2 raised similarity 0.627 to 0.805 but to prompt 11 lowered it 0.738 to 0.675. Convex-hull novelty was lower for few-shot sets.
limits: GPT-3 (old model). Few-shot raised similarity to human ideas but cut diversity. Prompt effects were inconsistent across problems.
agent_relevance: Prompt words like 'diverse' do not reliably widen the space; mechanism-level diversity steps are needed. Few-shot examples anchor, which echoes fixation.

source: Haase and Hanel (2023) Artificial muses: generative AI chatbots have risen to human-level creativity
finding: On the Alternative Uses Test, six chatbots matched the mean originality of 100 humans. Chatbots produced 2-3 times more ideas, but fluency and originality were unrelated. GPT-4 was best.
numbers: 100 humans vs 5 chatbots on 5 objects. Human-rated: B=-0.21, SE .15, p=.218; AI-rated: B=-0.18, p=.241. Averaged over prompts 32.8 humans beat the best of the five chatbots; 9.4 of 100 beat GPT-4 (AI-rated only). Rater ICC .85-.94; human-AI r .78-.94.
limits: Divergent thinking test, not design. Originality only, no usefulness. Chatbot sample of 5-6 is tiny.
agent_relevance: Shows plain divergence is easy for LLMs. The harder designerly part is the problem-framing and constraint judgement, which this task does not test.

source: Xu, Martelaro, McComb (2026) Supervising Ralph Wiggum: a metacognitive co-regulation agentic AI loop for engineering design
finding: Gemini 3.1 Pro design agents on battery pack design. A plain retry-until-valid loop (RWL) was compared with a self-regulating loop (SRL) and a loop where a second agent monitors the designer's metacognition (CRDAL). CRDAL designs were best at equal step cost. Authors frame fixation as an AI failure that mirrors human designers.
numbers: 30 runs per system. Mean capacity (Ah): RWL 72.07 (SD 20.52), SRL 106.08 (45.60), CRDAL 141.17 (48.45). ANOVA F(2,86)=21.606, p<.001, partial eta2 .334. RWL vs CRDAL d=1.846; RWL vs SRL d=0.956; SRL vs CRDAL d=0.746 (p=.005). Steps 9.07/9.10/9.37 (F=0.031, p=.97). Cells above 6048: RWL 0/29, SRL 9/30, CRDAL 20/30. RWL 29/30 valid.
limits: One task, one model, one temperature (1.0, high thinking). Larger variance in the two new systems. Smaller models untested.
agent_relevance: Closest match to our need: a design-theory idea (fixation, reflection-in-action) turned into an agent loop with a measured gain of about 2x over plain retry at no step cost. Separate monitor beat self-monitor: supports an independent reviewer operator.

source: Xu et al. (2026) same paper, reflection link
finding: The loop design ties Schon's reflection-in-action and on-action to LLM self-reflection and uses an external validator for success, not the agent's own judgement. A Progress Analyzer tool shows trajectory and trend to the designer.
numbers: Max 30 design steps per run; 30 seeds; no memory across runs.
quote: The reflective process is also analogically similar to how designers are theorized to work
limits: Mechanism details from the paper text; ablating the Progress Analyzer alone was not reported.
agent_relevance: Pattern to copy: external check decides success; a second agent reads the trajectory and proposes strategy, not another candidate.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) AutoTRIZ: automating engineering innovation with TRIZ and LLMs
finding: GPT-4 follows the TRIZ chain (contradiction, principles, solutions) and writes a reasoned report. Contradiction detection matched textbook expert analysis in 7 of 10 cases within top 3. A battery cooling design built from its output improved energy density 20-30% and cooling efficiency over 60%.
numbers: 10 textbook cases; 7/10 complete or half match in top-3 detections. Output varied run to run (entropy used; self-consistency suggested). BTMS result: efficiency up more than 60%, grouping efficiency and density 20-30%. One co-author verified, no blind expert panel.
limits: Expert match is not a gold standard. Case study is one problem, author-designed follow-up.
agent_relevance: A prescriptive design method can be wrapped as a fixed multi-step LLM pipeline with interpretable output. Link to the TRIZ subfield (not covered here).

source: Wen et al. (2026) Exploration vs. fixation: scaffolding divergent and convergent thinking (HAICo)
finding: A two-mode system (diverge on remote ideas via associative prompting, then converge on refinement), based on the Geneplore model, beat ChatGPT on creativity support, novelty and diversity in a within-subjects study.
numbers: N=24, Wilcoxon signed-rank. CSI all 5 dimensions higher (p<.002). Usability UMUX-Lite 81.25 vs 64.24 (p<.001). Image clusters 2.88 vs 2.04 (p=.021). Self-reported learning 5.29 vs 3.12 (p<.001). Fewer refinement prompts per cluster. 5 non-author raters scored 123 images.
limits: One poster task, students, self-report heavy, compared against a bare ChatGPT chatbot rather than another scaffold.
agent_relevance: A forced diverge-then-converge mode switch is a measurable improvement over a one-shot chatbot. Supports separate explore and commit states.

source: Kocaballi et al. (2026) Drag or traction: how designers appropriate friction in AI ideation outputs
finding: Deliberately fragmenting, delaying or obscuring AI output made designers treat it as raw material (Schon's materials that talk back) instead of a finished answer. Effect depended on a person trait, tolerance for ambiguity.
numbers: 6 designers, qualitative, seamless vs friction conditions. No effect sizes.
limits: Very small, no quantitative test; moderator 'friction disposition' is a proposal only.
agent_relevance: Weak but relevant: for our agent, presenting its own candidates as unfinished material to critique may reduce lock-in. Needs testing.

source: Chen et al. (2026) NexusAI: design space exploration through cognitive abstraction and functional decomposition
finding: Breaks LLM ideas into typed What-How-Value fragments at four abstraction levels so designers can recombine them. Reported better design space exploration and lower cognitive load than a baseline.
numbers: Formative study 7 designers; evaluation N=14 within-subjects. Detailed statistics not read (abstract and intro only).
limits: Only abstract and intro read. Small n.
agent_relevance: Decomposing ideas into function parts and abstracting them is a concrete way to make the design space explicit for an LLM loop.

source: Jiang, Hu, Wood, Luo (2021) Data-driven design-by-analogy: state of the art and future directions
finding: Survey of data-driven design-by-analogy sorted into encoding, retrieval, mapping and evaluation. Notes analogy helps reduce fixation.
numbers: 47 papers in final literature set.
limits: Pre-LLM-era survey (2021).
agent_relevance: Older AI line: analogy retrieval over design databases. Gives the lineage for retrieval-based design agents.

source: Maher and Poon (1996) Modelling design exploration as co-evolution
finding: Early computational model of problem-solution co-evolution using genetic ideas, cited as the first machine version of what Dorst and Cross later described in humans.
numbers: Not read; cited in Guo et al. 2024 (read).
limits: Known only through citation in c01.
agent_relevance: Shows the co-evolution idea began as an AI algorithm, so putting it back into an agent loop is a return, not a novelty.

source: Dorst and Cross (2001) Creativity in the design process: co-evolution of problem-solution
finding: Observed nine experienced industrial designers; creative moments came when a problem frame and a solution idea matched, after repeated moves between the two. Used as the reference model by every LLM study above.
numbers: Not read this session; described from citations in c01 and c03.
limits: Small protocol study with expert designers on one task.
agent_relevance: The definition of the operator we want: alternate between reframing and candidate generation until they fit.

source: Cross (1982) Designerly ways of knowing (Design Studies)
finding: Founding claim that design has its own way of knowing, centred on solution-first working, ill-defined problems, constructive thinking and use of sketches and models. Not directly tested on LLMs in any paper read.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: No LLM study read cites it as the tested hypothesis; they use later co-evolution work.
agent_relevance: Gap: nobody has tested whether LLMs show 'solution-first' behaviour. Zhang 2025 (c03) is the closest.

source: Gap note: searches for LLM tests of Schon reflection-in-action and Lawson/Cross experiments
finding: Arxiv listing searches (design fixation, design thinking, co-evolution, LLM design) returned the studies above and no replication of Cross 1982 or Lawson's block-problem study with LLMs. APIs (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, export.arxiv) were rate-limited, so the sweep is partial.
numbers: About 6 arXiv listing pages, 2 web searches.
limits: Search coverage incomplete; absence is not proof.
agent_relevance: The open ground is a design-cognition benchmark (problem framing, fixation, co-evolution moves) for LLM agents.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Fixation in GenAI, interview theme on experts vs novices
finding: Experienced designers critically evaluated and often rejected ChatGPT suggestions; novices adopted them with little change and fed ChatGPT text into Midjourney unedited.
numbers: Only 2 participants edited the Midjourney prompt independently; most pasted unmodified.
limits: Anecdotes from 10 participants.
agent_relevance: Human-in-loop quality depends on critique skill; an agent should carry an explicit critique step, since novice-style acceptance amplifies AI fixation.

source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) qualitative finding: prompt as fixation source
finding: Authors found the written brief and the initial example both fixed the prompts people wrote, so the AI inherited and amplified the anchor. Value depended on how people phrased prompts and used outputs.
numbers: Qualitative analysis within the N=60 study; 3 phases analysed (brief to prompt, example to prompt, images to sketch).
limits: Interpretive.
agent_relevance: Strip or vary the anchoring example when prompting; generate from several framings of the brief.

source: Ma et al. (2023) design-space coverage finding
finding: GPT-3 output had much lower variance across solutions than crowd output, which ranged from absurd to practical. Lower variance went with lower novelty.
numbers: Convex-hull volumes per prompt roughly 0.09-0.45 across conditions (table read); crowd higher on novelty on the expert scale.
limits: Single model generation, no temperature study.
agent_relevance: Diversity must be enforced through sampling many framings or agents, as one stream converges.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) limit on LLM nonlinearity and suggested fixes
finding: Authors state LLM design processes have far lower evolutionary complexity and adaptability than humans and propose fine-tuning on real design data or Graph of Thoughts for retrospection and parallel exploration.
numbers: No tested numbers for the fixes.
limits: Proposal only.
agent_relevance: Check whether a loop with explicit revisit-of-problem steps raises PS and SP transition counts. That is a testable metric for our schema.

source: Xu et al. (2026) trajectory in latent design space
finding: CRDAL ended in a different region of the embedded design space and pushed cell counts up; the plain loop stayed under 6048 cells in all runs.
numbers: RWL 29/29 under 6048 cells; SRL 21/30 under; CRDAL 20/30 over, mode 8100 cells (6/30).
limits: Latent-space plot is descriptive.
agent_relevance: A diversity or coverage metric over trajectories can show whether a monitor really broadens search.
